content.comment_body: Has anyone tried using [url] yet? It appears to be a promising solution for communicating with a network of [product_name] devices, particularly if it can interact with [version_no] controllers. I'm looking for experiences specifically regarding connections to [product_name].

Hello, I've seen this software before; it functions as a graphics editor. From what I can tell, it's intended only for [version_no] controllers, utilizing the [product_name] Box hardware for routing. It's not designed for use with [product_name]. Here's the general workflow: [version_no] PLC >>> [product_name] Box >>> SCADA server with SQL database >>> [product_name] Box >>> mobile devices. I don’t see much benefit in using it under these conditions. If it only benefits the [version_no] series, here's an alternative: [version_no] PLC >>> SCADA server with SQL database >>> mobile devices >>> [version_no] PLC, or direct connection using Bluetooth/WiFi and Android. Again, it is not suitable for [product_name]. Regards,

Support from [url] says: "[product_name] fully supports [version_no] controllers from [company_name]. There is limited compatibility with [product_name] (only supporting Input, Output(Q), and Flag memory(M) registers), and only basic testing has been done; flawless operation isn't guaranteed. Full protocol support is planned by the end of the year." My understanding is: [product_name] >>> [product_name] box (Webserver/GUI) >>> Router >>> Internet for remote access with improved graphics, or [product_name] >>> iPad HMI app if on the same network.

Hi, I wonder why I would need both the [product_name] box and server when some programming on a regular PC may accomplish the same purpose. It feels somewhat convoluted, similar to connecting DEVICE1->RS232->RS485->RS232->DEVICE2. Regards,

Hi, I've implemented [product_name] in a few projects. It is a comprehensive SCADA platform with typical client-server setup: install [product_name] on a server, then deliver web-based access to clients. Communication with [version_no] controllers is seamless. The graphical interface is high quality, and overall, I'm very satisfied as there are more options compared to [product_name].

I've used [product_name] myself. My setup utilizes [product_name], in conjunction with a Raspberry Pi serving as the SCADA server. It operates reliably with [product_name]. I'm pleased with the overall performance, and the licensing costs are reasonable. I've noticed that the [product_name] support forum doesn’t get much activity, though the documentation available on their website is fairly good.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants review integrating [product_name], a third-party SCADA application, with both [product_name] and [version_no] controllers. Initial feedback expresses concerns about compatibility and complexity, especially for [product_name], due to limited support and indirect setup. Subsequent comments from users with hands-on experience highlight positive outcomes—praising graphical capability, adaptable client-server architecture, and successful deployment with [product_name] and [version_no] controllers. Documentation is described as sufficient, but active community support is lacking.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for a reliable, comprehensive third-party tool that provides seamless connectivity and full feature compatibility for [product_name] and [version_no] controllers, paired with straightforward setup and a modern interface. Reasonable licensing fees and solid documentation or responsive community support are also important.
